summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book, Ray is confronted by Chief Becker about a child's murder aboard a ship. Becker insists the Lilaikens, a political terrorist group, are not responsible, since the killing lacks a rational purpose and the body was mutilated. Ray protests that the case is outside his assignment and that he lacks the training, but Becker says Captain Sorensen has already arranged the reassignment through CIU, pulling in favors so Ray will lead the investigation.
one_line: Ray Becker-style standoff: Chief Becker orders Ray to take over a child's murder investigation aboard a ship, despite Ray's objections.
key_facts: Becker argues the Lilaikens would not have mutilated the body or disposed of it so carelessly if the kid had some kind of target value.
Becker describes the Lilaikens as political terrorists, not monsters.
Becker asks rhetorically what message the Lilaikens would send by hacking up kids, calling the idea untenable.
Ray says the investigation is not part of his assignment and refuses it flatly.
Becker tells Ray that the lead on the investigation is being made part of his assignment as of now.
Ray says he does not have the training for the job and that two weeks out from New Holyoke the chances of making suitable progress are close to nil.
Becker says the decision was made by Sorensen, the captain.
Ray says his superiors will not tolerate interference with his primary objectives.
Becker says the captain has already consented with superiors and called in a raft of favors with CIU.
Ray had earlier said he had all but confirmed the ship is clean.
Becker notes Ray has the freedom to investigate anonymously so passengers are not frightened by security officers banging on their doors.
Ray notes that the incident is less rational than blowing up starships, a remark Becker answers with a rebuke about the Lilaikens.
